account: Court reporting describes an OpenAI emergency disclosure that reached the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office through the FBI after Darren Zhou wrote threats against his ex-girlfriend in ChatGPT. Deputies compared those messages with anonymous threats that she had preserved. The sheriff’s booking entry lists May 29, 2026 as his arrest date. BocaNewsNow reports that he pleaded guilty on August 13 to written threats, aggravated stalking, and unlawful use of a two-way communication device. Adjudication was withheld, with eight years of probation, two years of GPS monitoring, and restrictions on contact and weapons. The accessible reporting cites court documents but does not reproduce the complete affidavit or plea order. It supports a police intervention and court restrictions, rather than proof that an attack would otherwise have occurred.

ai_role.statement: The reporting identifies an OpenAI disclosure as the route that brought Zhou’s messages to police attention. OpenAI’s general policy describes detection followed by human review before possible referral to law enforcement. That policy does not document the exact classifier, trigger, reviewer decisions, or ChatGPT replies in this case.

fields.account: Court reporting describes an OpenAI emergency disclosure that reached the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office through the FBI after Darren Zhou wrote threats against his ex-girlfriend in ChatGPT. Deputies compared those messages with anonymous threats that she had preserved. The sheriff’s booking entry lists May 29, 2026 as his arrest date. BocaNewsNow reports that he pleaded guilty on August 13 to written threats, aggravated stalking, and unlawful use of a two-way communication device. Adjudication was withheld, with eight years of probation, two years of GPS monitoring, and restrictions on contact and weapons. The accessible reporting cites court documents but does not reproduce the complete affidavit or plea order. It supports a police intervention and court restrictions, rather than proof that an attack would otherwise have occurred.

fields.account: Court reporting describes an OpenAI emergency disclosure that reached the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office through the FBI after Darren Zhou wrote threats against his ex-girlfriend in ChatGPT. Deputies compared those messages with anonymous threats that she had preserved. The sheriff’s booking entry lists May 29, 2026 as his arrest date. BocaNewsNow reports that he pleaded guilty on August 13 to written threats, aggravated stalking, and unlawful use of a two-way communication device. Adjudication was withheld, with eight years of probation, two years of GPS monitoring, and restrictions on contact and weapons. The accessible reporting cites court documents but does not reproduce the complete affidavit or plea order. It supports a police intervention and court restrictions, rather than proof that an attack would otherwise have occurred.

purpose: OpenAI says that when it detects users planning to harm others, it routes the conversations to a small team trained on its usage policies. It says that if human reviewers find an imminent threat of serious physical harm to others, it may refer the case to law enforcement. This referral is that designed use. ChatGPT itself is a general-purpose assistant, which Zhou used to rehearse his plans.
